data.narrative:
Cortical Labs is a Series A AI & Software company founded by Hon Weng Chong and Andy Kitchen that has raised $11M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparison set of 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage peers—Reflection AI ($25.0B Series A), Together AI ($8.3B Series A), Physical Intelligence ($5.6B Series B), and Black Forest Labs ($3.2B Series B)—supplemented by a broader private comps universe of 8 companies and 1 public reference (Palantir, PLTR).

Two triangulation methods prove applicable. Stage-Progression methodology applies a 2.0x multiplier to the $11M raised proxy, implying a $22M valuation. Peer-Median analysis uses the median valuation across the 4-company comp set, yielding $7.0B, with a range spanning $3.2B (floor) to $25.0B (ceiling). The wide peer range reflects significant dispersion in recent AI & Software valuations at this stage.

The triangulated analysis supports a range from $19M (low) to $8.0B (high), with a median of $3.5B. The Stage-Progression method implies material undervaluation relative to peer medians, while Peer-Median dominates the synthesis given the direct comparability of the sample. Key uncertainties include Cortical Labs' revenue trajectory, capital efficiency relative to peers, and the sustainability of frontier-AI valuations in the current environment. Absent additional product-market or financial metrics, the $3.5B median represents the central estimate.
